text:
Jordan K: @deploy-bot blocked RC2 release (2026-03-18 RC2). Reason: SBOM provenance mismatch + vuln-scan reported 2 high findings. Who's owning triage?

deploy-bot: [automated] Release RC2 blocked — checks failing: sbom-provenance, vuln-scan. CI: https://ci.internal/redwood/releases/RC2-201823

security-bot: Vuln scan summary:
- CVE-2025-4321 (High) in transitive dep 'fastparser' <=1.2.3 via shared-lib@2.0.0
- CVE-2026-0001 (High) in 'jsonify' 0.9.7 via shared-lib@2.0.0
Recommendation: pin shared-lib to 2.0.3 (contains backport) or rollback release.

Diego Ramos: SBOM provenance details: build image digest used: sha256:abc123, allowed digest in policy: sha256:def456. Provenance check flagged the mismatch. Likely local builder cache used a different base.

Maya Li: I can put together a hotpatch: bump shared-lib to 2.0.3 and jsonify to 0.9.8, plus rebuild with pinned base image digest. Estimated time ~45-60m for build + canary.

Priya Patel: Security side: we can accept pin+patch IF the canary includes the regression tests for those CVEs and we capture SBOM provenance proof for the build. Also need a short rationale for the release notes.

Samir Khan: Legal/compliance note: if we change the base image digest, we must document the reason in the release changelog and attach the signed SBOM. They want traceability for the rebuild.

Alice Chen: ops: change-window policy allows a 1-hour exception for hotfixes with canary if oncall and security approve. @oncall-eng please ack and, if ok, approve temporary change-window.

oncall-eng: ack — oncall available. Approving timeboxed 90m window for mitigation work and canary. Please tag me when canary begins.

Jordan K: Proposed plan (timeboxed):
1) Pin base image to sha256:def456 in build config (addresses provenance mismatch).
2) Bump shared-lib -> 2.0.3 and jsonify -> 0.9.8, run vulnerability regression tests.
3) Rebuild artifacts, publish SBOMs, run canary (10% traffic).
4) If canary green + vuln tests pass -> lift deploy hold and proceed.
5) If rebuild fails or new issues -> rollback to RC1 and open incident.
Estimated wall time: 90 minutes. Vote?

Maya Li: +1
Priya Patel: +1 from security assuming regression tests are included and SBOM provenance is captured
Diego Ramos: I'll update the build configs now and push a branch.

Jordan K: Command to trigger: `./scripts/release-rebuild --pin-base=sha256:def456 --deps=shared-lib@2.0.3,jsonify@0.9.8`

deploy-bot: Acknowledged. Rebuild started (job 4521). Logs: https://ci.internal/redwood/jobs/4521

security-bot: Reminder: after build completes, attach signed SBOM and provenance link. Use tool: `sbom-tool sign --artifact=rc2.tar.gz --kms=prod-kms`.

Diego Ramos: Build finished, artifact published. SBOM signed and uploaded: https://ci.internal/artifacts/rc2-4521/sbom.json.sig

Maya Li: Kicking off canary now (10% traffic). Monitoring dashboards -> https://dash.ops/redwood/canary/rc2-4521

security-bot: Quick check: vuln-regression tests ran, fixed CVE tests passed. No new high findings in scan v2.

Jordan K: Canary looks stable at +8m. @oncall-eng please confirm no latency regressions.

oncall-eng: observed no latency or error increases in the canary window. Good to proceed if security ok.

Priya Patel: Confirmed. SBOM provenance attached and hash matches. Security approves lifting the hold.

Jordan K: Proceeding to lift deploy hold and continue release. Action: deploy-bot, promote RC2 -> stable.

deploy-bot: Promotion started. Release RC2 promoted to stable. Notes: base-image pinned, deps bumped, SBOM signed. Release notes draft: "Hotfix: address transitive CVEs CVE-2025-4321, CVE-2026-0001; pinned base image digest for provenance."

Samir Khan: Filing a short post-release note for compliance with links to SBOM and signed artifacts. I'll open the doc.

Jordan K: Thanks everyone. If anything else pops, we revert to RC1 and open incident. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [automated] Thread closed: release promoted.
